{'id': '80e032c2', 'parent_ids': [], 'type': 'Tool Call', 'content': {'tool_name': 'read_file', 'tool_arguments': {'arg_0': './schema_check.py'}, 'tool_output': 'import sqlite3\nimport json\n\nconn = sqlite3.connect(\'world.db\')\nc = conn.cursor()\n\n# List all tables\nc.execute("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type=\'table\'")\ntables = [r[0] for r in c.fetchall()]\nprint("Tables:", tables)\n\n# For each table, show columns and row count\nfor t in tables:\n    c.execute(f"PRAGMA table_info({t})")\n    cols = [(r[1], r[2]) for r in c.fetchall()]\n    c.execute(f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM {t}")\n    cnt = c.fetchone()[0]\n    print(f"\\n=== {t} ({cnt} rows) ===")\n    for name, typ in cols:\n        print(f"  {name} ({typ})")\n\n# Sample flight row with full detail\nc.execute("SELECT * FROM flights LIMIT 1")\nfcols = [d[0] for d in c.description]\nrow = c.fetchone()\nif row:\n    print("\\n=== Sample flight row ===")\n    for col, val in zip(fcols, row):\n        sv = str(val)[:400] if val else "NULL"\n        print(f"  {col}: {sv}")\n\n# Unique airports\nc.execute("SELECT DISTINCT origin FROM flights")\norigins = sorted([r[0] for r in c.fetchall() if r[0]])\nc.execute("SELECT DISTINCT destination FROM flights")\ndests = sorted([r[0] for r in c.fetchall() if r[0]])\nprint(f"\\nOrigins: {origins}")\nprint(f"Destinations: {dests}")\n\n# LHR flights\nc.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM flights WHERE origin=\'LHR\' OR destination=\'LHR\'")\nprint(f"Flights involving LHR: {c.fetchone()[0]}")\n\n# Sample reservation\ntry:\n    c.execute("SELECT * FROM reservations LIMIT 1")\n    rcols = [d[0] for d in c.description]\n    rrow = c.fetchone()\n    if rrow:\n        print("\\n=== Sample reservation ===")\n        for col, val in zip(rcols, rrow):\n            sv = str(val)[:400] if val else "NULL"\n            print(f"  {col}: {sv}")\nexcept Exception as e:\n    print(f"No reservations table: {e}")\n\nconn.close()\n'}}

{'id': '20bf559e', 'parent_ids': [], 'type': 'Tool Call', 'content': {'tool_name': 'read_file', 'tool_arguments': {'arg_0': './workspace/docs/q3_report.md'}, 'tool_output': '# Meridian Analytics — Q3 2026 Business Report\n\n**Period:** July 1 – September 7, 2026\n**Prepared by:** Rachel Kim, VP of Sales | Claire Fontaine, CFO\n**Distribution:** Executive Team\n\n---\n\n## Executive Summary\n\nQ3 2026 marks another strong quarter for Meridian Analytics. Across our 15-person team we\nclosed 14 deals out of 22 opportunities, generating **$1,040,000** in new\ncontract value. The sales pipeline remains healthy with several high-value deals in the\npending stage. Customer support ticket volume held steady, with critical issues resolved\nsame-day in all cases.\n\n---\n\n## Sales Performance\n\nTotal closed revenue for the quarter reached **$1,040,000**, with the **South**\nregion leading all territories at **$468,000** in won deals. Our three-person\nfield sales team — James Okafor, Sofia Delgado, and Marcus Webb — collectively worked\n22 active opportunities during the period.\n\nProduct mix shifted toward Meridian Insights Pro, which accounted for the majority of\nclosed revenue. Meridian DataBridge continues to serve as a strong land-and-expand vehicle\nwith several upsell opportunities maturing in Q4.\n\nWin rate for the quarter stood at **63.6%**, slightly above the company\ntarget of 55%. Three deals totalling approximately $240,000 remain in pending status and\nare expected to close by end of September.\n\n---\n\n## Key Highlights\n\n- **Top deal:** Sofia Delgado closed a $198,000 Meridian Insights Pro contract with a\n  Southern-region enterprise customer on September 5 (D019).\n- **Team headcount:** Meridian Analytics closes Q3 at 15 employees across five departments:\n  Sales (4), Engineering (5), Product (3), HR (1), and Finance (2).\n- **Support SLA:** All critical-priority tickets (TKT-004, TKT-011, TKT-015) were resolved\n  within 24 hours of creation.\n- **License utilisation:** SKU-001 (Meridian Insights Pro) is at 94% capacity — a\n  procurement review is scheduled for October.\n\n---\n\n## Next Steps\n\n1. Close the three pending deals (D007, D013, D020, D022) before Q3 end.\n2. Begin Q4 pipeline review — target $1.2M in new ARR.\n3. Resolve the open support tickets (TKT-013, TKT-016, TKT-019) ahead of quarterly\n   customer success calls.\n4. Conduct a license capacity review for SKU-001 and SKU-003 in early October.\n5. HR to initiate two new engineering hire approvals with Kenji Obi to support Q4 roadmap.\n'}}
{'id': '611b8879', 'parent_ids': [], 'type': 'Tool Call', 'content': {'tool_name': 'read_file', 'tool_arguments': {'arg_0': './workspace/docs/meeting_notes_2026_09.txt'}, 'tool_output': 'Q3 REVIEW MEETING — MEETING NOTES\n==================================\nDate:      Monday, September 8, 2026\nTime:      10:00 – 11:30 am PT (Zoom)\nFacilitator: Rachel Kim\n\nATTENDEES\n---------\nRachel Kim        (VP of Sales)\nClaire Fontaine   (CFO)\nPriya Nair        (CTO)\nHannah Park       (Head of Product)\nKenji Obi         (HR Manager)\nJames Okafor      (Account Executive)\nSofia Delgado     (Account Executive)\nDaniel Torres     (Product Manager)\nOscar Mensah      (Finance Analyst)\n\nAGENDA\n------\n1. Q3 Sales Review\n2. Engineering & Product Update\n3. Finance Snapshot\n4. HR Update\n5. Action Items / Q4 Planning\n\n---\n\n1. Q3 SALES REVIEW\n-------------------\nRachel Kim opened with a summary of Q3 performance.\n\n- Total revenue closed (won deals): $1,040,000 across 14 closed-won deals.\n- 22 total deals worked in the quarter; win rate 63.6%.\n- South region led all territories at $468,000 in closed revenue.\n- Largest single deal: D019 — Sofia Delgado — $198,000 — Meridian Insights Pro\n  (signed September 5, Southern enterprise account).\n- Pipeline carry-over into Q4: D007 ($7,800), D013 ($105,000), D020 ($115,000),\n  D022 ($11,000) — total pending ~$239,300.\n\nJames Okafor noted that the North region pipeline is especially strong heading into Q4,\nwith two new prospects from the BostonTech conference (see EX001 travel expense).\n\nAction: Rachel to circulate updated forecast by EOD September 9.\n\n2. ENGINEERING & PRODUCT UPDATE\n---------------------------------\nPriya Nair reported that the DataBridge connector reached 28/30 license utilisation\n(SKU-003) and a capacity upgrade is under evaluation for Q4.\n\nHannah Park flagged that Custom Dashboard Builder (SKU-009) is at 22/25 seats; renewal\nin February 2027 should include a seat expansion.\n\nDaniel Torres confirmed the new Meridian Connector - REST (SKU-005) rollout is complete.\nEleven of twenty available licenses are now provisioned.\n\nThree open support tickets (TKT-013, TKT-016, TKT-019) were reviewed. Liam Chen and\nTom Reyes are owners; target closure by September 12.\n\n3. FINANCE SNAPSHOT\n--------------------\nClaire Fontaine presented a brief Q3 finance summary.\n\n- Five unapproved expense items remain outstanding (EX005, EX010, EX012, EX020, EX023,\n  EX025). Total: ~$1,050. Oscar Mensah to chase approvals by September 10.\n- Hardware spend is tracking within budget. SKU-013 (HIPAA Compliance Pack) renews\n  October 31 at $15,000 — renewal decision needed by September 26.\n\n4. HR UPDATE\n-------------\nKenji Obi confirmed headcount is stable at 15. Two engineering hire requisitions will be\nsubmitted to the board in Q4 to support the roadmap expansion outlined by Priya.\n\nNew joiner orientation materials (see onboarding_guide.md) have been refreshed for the\nupdated tool stack.\n\n5. ACTION ITEMS\n----------------\n| Owner           | Action                                              | Due          |\n|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------------|--------------|\n| Rachel Kim      | Circulate updated Q4 sales forecast                 | Sep 9, 2026  |\n| Oscar Mensah    | Chase outstanding expense approvals (EX005 et al.)  | Sep 10, 2026 |\n| Liam Chen       | Close TKT-013, TKT-016                              | Sep 12, 2026 |\n| Tom Reyes       | Close TKT-019, TKT-020                              | Sep 12, 2026 |\n| Hannah Park     | Initiate SKU-003 capacity upgrade request           | Sep 15, 2026 |\n| Claire Fontaine | Prepare HIPAA pack renewal decision memo (SKU-013)  | Sep 26, 2026 |\n| Kenji Obi       | Submit Q4 engineering hire requisitions             | Oct 1, 2026  |\n\nNEXT MEETING: Q4 Kick-off — Monday, October 6, 2026, 10:00 am PT\n'}}
{'id': '57cba57d', 'parent_ids': [], 'type': 'Tool Call', 'content': {'tool_name': 'read_file', 'tool_arguments': {'arg_0': './workspace/docs/onboarding_guide.md'}, 'tool_output': '# Meridian Analytics — Employee Onboarding Guide\n\nWelcome to Meridian Analytics! This guide covers everything you need for a smooth first\nweek. If anything is unclear, reach out to your manager or HR.\n\n---\n\n## Day 1 Setup\n\n### Accounts & Access\n- [ ] Receive your Meridian email (`<firstname>.<lastname>@meridiananalytics.io`) from IT\n- [ ] Set up Google Workspace (Gmail, Calendar, Drive)\n- [ ] Activate your Slack account and join `#general`, `#engineering`, `#announcements`\n- [ ] Log in to the Meridian Analytics platform at `app.meridiananalytics.io`\n- [ ] Set up 1Password (password manager) — your vault invite arrives by email\n- [ ] Enable MFA on all company accounts before Day 2\n\n### Physical / Badge\n- [ ] Collect your office keycard from Kenji Obi (HR Manager) — desk 4B, second floor\n- [ ] Sign the equipment acceptance form for your assigned laptop\n- [ ] Take a building safety briefing with the office manager\n\n### Tools to Install\n| Tool | Purpose |\n|------|---------|\n| Slack | Team communication |\n| Zoom | Video calls |\n| GitHub | Source code (Engineering) |\n| Figma | Design collaboration (Product/Engineering) |\n| Notion | Internal documentation |\n\n---\n\n## Week 1 Tasks\n\n- [ ] 1:1 with your direct manager (Day 1, 30 min)\n- [ ] Team introduction call — attend `#standup` at 9:30 am daily\n- [ ] Read the Company Handbook in Notion (link shared on Day 1)\n- [ ] Complete Security Awareness training (mandatory, ~45 min)\n- [ ] Complete GDPR & Data Handling training (mandatory, ~30 min)\n- [ ] Shadow a colleague in your team for half a day\n- [ ] Submit your signed offer letter copy and ID documents to Kenji Obi\n- [ ] Set up your direct deposit and benefits enrolment in Rippling (deadline: Day 5)\n\n---\n\n## Key Contacts\n\n| Name | Role | Department | Email |\n|------|------|------------|-------|\n| Kenji Obi | HR Manager | HR | k.obi@meridiananalytics.io |\n| Priya Nair | CTO | Engineering | p.nair@meridiananalytics.io |\n| Rachel Kim | VP of Sales | Sales | r.kim@meridiananalytics.io |\n| Hannah Park | Head of Product | Product | h.park@meridiananalytics.io |\n| Claire Fontaine | CFO | Finance | c.fontaine@meridiananalytics.io |\n\nFor IT issues: open a ticket in the `#it-help` Slack channel.\n\n---\n\n## Policies Summary\n\n- **Working hours:** Core hours are 10 am – 4 pm local time. Flexible outside these times.\n- **Expenses:** Submit expenses within 30 days of purchase via Ramp. Meals > $75 require\n  prior approval. Hardware purchases > $300 require manager sign-off.\n- **PTO:** 20 days per year (accrued monthly). Submit requests in Rippling ≥ 5 business\n  days in advance for planned leave.\n- **Remote work:** Fully remote-friendly. Office available Tuesday–Thursday.\n- **Confidentiality:** All employees sign an NDA on Day 1. Do not share customer data,\n  deal information, or financial figures outside the company.\n- **Code of Conduct:** Reviewed during Week 1 training. Zero tolerance for harassment.\n\nFor the full policy list see the Company Handbook in Notion.\n'}}

{'id': '02613e2a', 'parent_ids': [], 'type': 'Tool Call', 'content': {'tool_name': 'read_file', 'tool_arguments': {'arg_0': './skills/tau2Airline/src/tau2/domains/airline/tools.py', 'start_line': '1', 'end_line': '80'}, 'tool_output': '"""Toolkit for the airline reservation system."""\n\nfrom copy import deepcopy\nfrom typing import List, Optional\n\nfrom loguru import logger\n\nfrom tau2.domains.airline.data_model import (\n    AirportCode,\n    AirportInfo,\n    CabinClass,\n    Certificate,\n    DirectFlight,\n    Flight,\n    FlightDateStatus,\n    FlightDateStatusAvailable,\n    FlightDB,\n    FlightInfo,\n    FlightType,\n    Insurance,\n    Passenger,\n    Payment,\n    Reservation,\n    ReservationFlight,\n    User,\n)\nfrom tau2.environment.toolkit import ToolKitBase, ToolType, is_tool\n\n# TODO: Add an abstract base class for the tools\n\n\nclass AirlineTools(ToolKitBase):  # Tools\n    """All the tools for the airline domain."""\n\n    db: FlightDB\n\n    def __init__(self, db: FlightDB) -> None:\n        super().__init__(db)\n\n    def _get_user(self, user_id: str) -> User:\n        """Get user from database."""\n        if user_id not in self.db.users:\n            raise ValueError(f"User {user_id} not found")\n        return self.db.users[user_id]\n\n    def _get_reservation(self, reservation_id: str) -> Reservation:\n        """Get reservation from database."""\n        if reservation_id not in self.db.reservations:\n            raise ValueError(f"Reservation {reservation_id} not found")\n        return self.db.reservations[reservation_id]\n\n    def _get_flight(self, flight_number: str) -> Flight:\n        """Get flight from database."""\n        if flight_number not in self.db.flights:\n            raise ValueError(f"Flight {flight_number} not found")\n        return self.db.flights[flight_number]\n\n    def _get_flight_instance(self, flight_number: str, date: str) -> FlightDateStatus:\n        """Get flight instance from database."""\n        flight = self._get_flight(flight_number)\n        if date not in flight.dates:\n            raise ValueError(f"Flight {flight_number} not found on date {date}")\n        return flight.dates[date]\n\n    def _get_flights_from_flight_infos(\n        self, flight_infos: List[FlightInfo]\n    ) -> list[FlightDateStatus]:\n        """Get the flight from the reservation."""\n        flights = []\n        for flight_info in flight_infos:\n            flights.append(\n                self._get_flight_instance(flight_info.flight_number, flight_info.date)\n            )\n        return flights\n\n    def _get_new_reservation_id(self) -> str:\n        """Get a new reservation id.\n        Assume each task makes at most 3 reservations\n\n        Returns:'}}
{'id': 'af599c2c', 'parent_ids': [], 'type': 'Tool Call', 'content': {'tool_name': 'read_file', 'tool_arguments': {'arg_0': './skills/tau2Airline/src/tau2/domains/airline/policy.md'}, 'tool_output': "# Airline Agent Policy\n\nThe current time is 2024-05-15 15:00:00 EST.\n\nAs an airline agent, you can help users **book**, **modify**, or **cancel** flight reservations. You also handle **refunds and compensation**.\n\nBefore taking any actions that update the booking database (booking, modifying flights, editing baggage, changing cabin class, or updating passenger information), you must list the action details and obtain explicit user confirmation (yes) to proceed.\n\nYou should not provide any information, knowledge, or procedures not provided by the user or available tools, or give subjective recommendations or comments.\n\nYou should only make one tool call at a time, and if you make a tool call, you should not respond to the user simultaneously. If you respond to the user, you should not make a tool call at the same time.\n\nYou should deny user requests that are against this policy.\n\nYou should transfer the user to a human agent if and only if the request cannot be handled within the scope of your actions. To transfer, first make a tool call to transfer_to_human_agents, and then send the message 'YOU ARE BEING TRANSFERRED TO A HUMAN AGENT. PLEASE HOLD ON.' to the user.\n\n## Domain Basic\n\n### User\nEach user has a profile containing:\n- user id\n- email\n- addresses\n- date of birth\n- payment methods\n- membership level\n- reservation numbers\n\nThere are three types of payment methods: **credit card**, **gift card**, **travel certificate**.\n\nThere are three membership levels: **regular**, **silver**, **gold**.\n\n### Flight\nEach flight has the following attributes:\n- flight number\n- origin\n- destination\n- scheduled departure and arrival time (local time)\n\nA flight can be available at multiple dates. For each date:\n- If the status is **available**, the flight has not taken off, available seats and prices are listed.\n- If the status is **delayed** or **on time**, the flight has not taken off, cannot be booked.\n- If the status is **flying**, the flight has taken off but not landed, cannot be booked.\n\nThere are three cabin classes: **basic economy**, **economy**, **business**. **basic economy** is its own class, completely distinct from **economy**.\n\nSeat availability and prices are listed for each cabin class.\n\n### Reservation\nEach reservation specifies the following:\n- reservation id\n- user id\n- trip type\n- flights\n- passengers\n- payment methods\n- created time\n- baggages\n- travel insurance information\n\nThere are two types of trip: **one way** and **round trip**.\n\n## Book flight\n\nThe agent must first obtain the user id from the user. \n\nThe agent should then ask for the trip type, origin, destination.\n\nCabin:\n- Cabin class must be the same across all the flights in a reservation. \n\nPassengers: \n- Each reservation can have at most five passengers. \n- The agent needs to collect the first name, last name, and date of birth for each passenger. \n- All passengers must fly the same flights in the same cabin.\n\nPayment: \n- Each reservation can use at most one travel certificate, at most one credit card, and at most three gift cards. \n- The remaining amount of a travel certificate is not refundable. \n- All payment methods must already be in user profile for safety reasons.\n\nChecked bag allowance: \n- If the booking user is a regular member:\n  - 0 free checked bag for each basic economy passenger\n  - 1 free checked bag for each economy passenger\n  - 2 free checked bags for each business passenger\n- If the booking user is a silver member:\n  - 1 free checked bag for each basic economy passenger\n  - 2 free checked bag for each economy passenger\n  - 3 free checked bags for each business passenger\n- If the booking user is a gold member:\n  - 2 free checked bag for each basic economy passenger\n  - 3 free checked bag for each economy passenger\n  - 4 free checked bags for each business passenger\n- Each extra baggage is 50 dollars.\n\nDo not add checked bags that the user does not need.\n\nTravel insurance: \n- The agent should ask if the user wants to buy the travel insurance.\n- The travel insurance is 30 dollars per passenger and enables full refund if the user needs to cancel the flight given health or weather reasons.\n\n## Modify flight\n\nFirst, the agent must obtain the user id and reservation id. \n- The user must provide their user id. \n- If the user doesn't know their reservation id, the agent should help locate it using available tools.\n\nChange flights: \n- Basic economy flights cannot be modified.\n- Other reservations can be modified without changing the origin, destination, and trip type.\n- Some flight segments can be kept, but their prices will not be updated based on the current price.\n- The API does not check these for the agent, so the agent must make sure the rules apply before calling the API!\n\nChange cabin: \n- Cabin cannot be changed if any flight in the reservation has already been flown.\n- In other cases, all reservations, including basic economy, can change cabin without changing the flights.\n- Cabin class must remain the same across all the flights in the same reservation; changing cabin for just one flight segment is not possible.\n- If the price after cabin change is higher than the original price, the user is required to pay for the difference.\n- If the price after cabin change is lower than the original price, the user is should be refunded the difference.\n\nChange baggage and insurance: \n- The user can add but not remove checked bags.\n- The user cannot add insurance after initial booking.\n\nChange passengers:\n- The user can modify passengers but cannot modify the number of passengers.\n- Even a human agent cannot modify the number of passengers.\n\nPayment: \n- If the flights are changed, the user needs to provide a single gift card or credit card for payment or refund method. The payment method must already be in user profile for safety reasons.\n\n## Cancel flight\n\nFirst, the agent must obtain the user id and reservation id. \n- The user must provide their user id. \n- If the user doesn't know their reservation id, the agent should help locate it using available tools.\n\nThe agent must also obtain the reason for cancellation (change of plan, airline cancelled flight, or other reasons)\n\nIf any portion of the flight has already been flown, the agent cannot help and transfer is needed.\n\nOtherwise, flight can be cancelled if any of the following is true:\n- The booking was made within the last 24 hrs\n- The flight is cancelled by airline\n- It is a business flight\n- The user has travel insurance and the reason for cancellation is covered by insurance.\n\nThe API does not check that cancellation rules are met, so the agent must make sure the rules apply before calling the API!\n\nRefund:\n- The refund will go to original payment methods within 5 to 7 business days.\n\n## Refunds and Compensation\nDo not proactively offer a compensation unless the user explicitly asks for one.\n\nDo not compensate if the user is regular member and has no travel insurance and flies (basic) economy.\n\nAlways confirms the facts before offering compensation.\n\nOnly compensate if the user is a silver/gold member or has travel insurance or flies business.\n\n- If the user complains about cancelled flights in a reservation, the agent can offer a certificate as a gesture after confirming the facts, with the amount being $100 times the number of passengers.\n\n- If the user complains about delayed flights in a reservation and wants to change or cancel the reservation, the agent can offer a certificate as a gesture after confirming the facts and changing or cancelling the reservation, with the amount being $50 times the number of passengers.\n\nDo not offer compensation for any other reason than the ones listed above."}}

import sys, json

from tau2.domains.airline.data_model import FlightDB

# Search return one-stop flights
returns = tools.search_onestop_flight(origin='LHR', destination='LOS', date='2024-07-20')

# Convert to serializable format
def flight_to_dict(f):
    if hasattr(f, 'model_dump'):
        return f.model_dump()
    elif hasattr(f, '__dict__'):
        return {k: str(v) for k, v in f.__dict__.items() if not k.startswith('_')}
    else:
        return str(f)

def process_results(results):
    processed = []
    if hasattr(results, 'data'):
        results = results.data
    if isinstance(results, str):
        return results
    if hasattr(results, '__iter__'):
        for item in results:
            if isinstance(item, (list, tuple)):
                pair = [flight_to_dict(leg) for leg in item]
                processed.append(pair)
            else:
                processed.append(flight_to_dict(item))
    return processed

out_data = process_results(outbound)
ret_data = process_results(returns)

output = {
    "outbound_flights": out_data,
    "return_flights": ret_data
}

print(json.dumps(output, indent=2, default=str))
"""

                    lines.append(f"    Leg {j}: {fn}  {origin} → {dest}")
                    lines.append(f"           Departure: {dep}")
                    lines.append(f"           Arrival:   {arr}")
                    lines.append(f"           Status:    {status}")
                    lines.append(f"           Economy Price: ${econ_price}")
                else:
                    lines.append(f"    Leg {j}: {leg}")
        else:
            lines.append(f"    {pair}")
        lines.append("")

lines.append("-" * 80)
lines.append("RETURN: London (LHR) → Lagos (LOS) — July 20, 2024")
lines.append("-" * 80)
lines.append("")

if not return_flights:
    lines.append("No one-stop flights found for this route and date.")
else:
    for i, pair in enumerate(return_flights, 1):
        lines.append(f"  Option {i}:")
        if isinstance(pair, list):
            for j, leg in enumerate(pair, 1):
                if isinstance(leg, dict):
                    fn = leg.get("flight_number", leg.get("flight_id", "N/A"))
                    origin = leg.get("origin", "N/A")
                    dest = leg.get("destination", "N/A")
                    dep = leg.get("departure_time", leg.get("scheduled_departure_time", leg.get("departure", "N/A")))
                    arr = leg.get("arrival_time", leg.get("scheduled_arrival_time", leg.get("arrival", "N/A")))
                    status = leg.get("status", "N/A")
                    prices = leg.get("prices", {})
                    if isinstance(prices, dict):
                        econ_price = prices.get("economy", prices.get("Economy", "N/A"))
                    else:
                        econ_price = "N/A"
                    lines.append(f"    Leg {j}: {fn}  {origin} → {dest}")
                    lines.append(f"           Departure: {dep}")
                    lines.append(f"           Arrival:   {arr}")
                    lines.append(f"           Status:    {status}")
                    lines.append(f"           Economy Price: ${econ_price}")
                else:
                    lines.append(f"    Leg {j}: {leg}")
        else:
            lines.append(f"    {pair}")
        lines.append("")

lines.append("=" * 80)
lines.append("NOTES:")
lines.append("  - Deal: D006 (Worth: $120,000)")
lines.append("  - All prices shown are per-passenger economy class fares per leg.")
lines.append("  - One-stop flights have a layover at a connecting airport.")
lines.append("  - To proceed with booking, a user ID and payment method are required.")
lines.append("=" * 80)

report_content = "\n".join(lines)
print(report_content[:2000])
print(f"\n... Total report length: {len(report_content)} chars")

        annots = obj.__annotations__
        patched = False
        if 'prices' in annots:
            annots['prices'] = Dict[str, int]
            patched = True
        if 'available_seats' in annots:
            annots['available_seats'] = Dict[str, int]
            patched = True
        if patched:
            models_to_patch.append(name)

print(f"Patched models: {models_to_patch}")

# Rebuild all patched models
for name in models_to_patch:

# Rebuild parent models

dm.FlightDB.model_rebuild(force=True)

from tau2.domains.airline.tools import AirlineTools
db = dm.FlightDB.load()

# Search return one-stop flights
ret = tools.search_onestop_flight(origin='LHR', destination='LOS', date='2024-07-20')

def serialize(obj):
    if hasattr(obj, 'model_dump'):
        return obj.model_dump()
    elif isinstance(obj, list):
        return [serialize(x) for x in obj]
    elif isinstance(obj, tuple):
        return [serialize(x) for x in obj]
    elif isinstance(obj, dict):
        return {k: serialize(v) for k, v in obj.items()}
    else:
        return str(obj)

out_data = serialize(outbound)
ret_data = serialize(ret)

result = {
    "outbound_flights": out_data,
    "return_flights": ret_data
}

with open('flight_search_results.json', 'w') as f:
    json.dump(result, f, indent=2, default=str)

print(json.dumps(result, indent=2, default=str)[:8000])
print("\\n--- SAVED TO flight_search_results.json ---")

        if isinstance(info, dict) and info.get('status') == 'available':
            econ = None

script = """import sqlite3
import json

conn = sqlite3.connect("world.db")
c = conn.cursor()
c.execute("PRAGMA table_info(flights)")
fcols = [r[1] for r in c.fetchall()]
c.execute("SELECT * FROM flights")
flights = []
for row in c.fetchall():
    d = dict(zip(fcols, row))
    for k, v in d.items():
        if isinstance(v, str) and v.strip().startswith("{"):
            try:
                d[k] = json.loads(v)
            except:
                pass
    flights.append(d)
conn.close()

by_origin = {}
for f in flights:
    by_origin.setdefault(f.get("origin", ""), []).append(f)

def avail(f):
    dd = f.get("dates", {})
    if not isinstance(dd, dict):
        return []
    r = []
    for dt, info in dd.items():
        if isinstance(info, dict) and info.get("status") == "available":
            r.append((dt, info.get("prices", {})))
    r.sort()
    return r

def pfmt(prices):
    if not isinstance(prices, dict):
        return "N/A"
    p = []
    for c in ["basic_economy","economy","premium_economy","business","first"]:
        if c in prices and prices[c] is not None:
            p.append(c.replace("_"," ").title() + ": $" + str(prices[c]))
    return " | ".join(p) if p else "N/A"

direct_out = [f for f in flights if f.get("origin")=="LOS" and f.get("destination")=="LHR"]
direct_ret = [f for f in flights if f.get("origin")=="LHR" and f.get("destination")=="LOS"]

onestop_out = []
for f1 in by_origin.get("LOS", []):
    hub = f1.get("destination", "")
    if hub == "LHR":
        continue
    for f2 in by_origin.get(hub, []):
        if f2.get("destination") == "LHR":
            d1 = {a[0] for a in avail(f1)}
            d2 = {a[0] for a in avail(f2)}
            cd = sorted(d1 & d2)
            if cd:
                onestop_out.append((f1, f2, cd))

onestop_ret = []
for f1 in by_origin.get("LHR", []):
    hub = f1.get("destination", "")
    if hub == "LOS":
        continue
    for f2 in by_origin.get(hub, []):
        if f2.get("destination") == "LOS":

            d2 = {a[0] for a in avail(f2)}
            cd = sorted(d1 & d2)
            if cd:
                onestop_ret.append((f1, f2, cd))

def finfo(f):
    return f.get("flight_id", f.get("id", "?"))

def airline(f):
    return f.get("airline", "?")

def dep(f):
    return f.get("scheduled_departure_time_est", "?")

def arr(f):

L.append("=" * 80)
L.append("")
L.append("Passenger:        James Okafor")
L.append("Trip Type:        Round Trip (One-Stop)")
L.append("Preferred Cabin:  Economy")
L.append("Time Preference:  Morning flights")
L.append("")
L.append("-" * 80)
L.append("OUTBOUND: Lagos (LOS) -> London Heathrow (LHR)")
L.append("-" * 80)
L.append("")

if direct_out:
    L.append("=== DIRECT FLIGHTS ===")
    L.append("")
    for f in direct_out:
        av = avail(f)
        L.append("Flight: " + finfo(f) + " | Airline: " + airline(f))
        L.append("  Departure: " + dep(f) + " | Arrival: " + arr(f))
        if av:
            L.append("  Available Dates (" + str(len(av)) + "):")
            for a in av[:10]:
                L.append("    " + a[0] + " - " + pfmt(a[1]))
            if len(av) > 10:

else:

                L.append("    ... and " + str(len(av)-10) + " more dates")
        else:
            L.append("  No available dates")
        L.append("")
else:
    L.append("No direct flights from LHR to LOS.")
    L.append("")

if onestop_ret:
    L.append("=== ONE-STOP CONNECTIONS ===")
    L.append("")
    for i, (f1, f2, dates) in enumerate(onestop_ret[:15]):
        hub = f1.get("destination", "?")
        av1 = avail(f1)
        av2 = avail(f2)
        p1 = av1[0][1] if av1 else {}
        p2 = av2[0][1] if av2 else {}
        L.append("Connection " + str(i+1) + ": LHR -> " + hub + " -> LOS")
        L.append("  Leg 1: " + finfo(f1) + " (" + airline(f1) + ") | Dep: " + dep(f1) + " | Arr: " + arr(f1))
        L.append("    Pricing: " + pfmt(p1))
        L.append("  Leg 2: " + finfo(f2) + " (" + airline(f2) + ") | Dep: " + dep(f2) + " | Arr: " + arr(f2))
        L.append("    Pricing: " + pfmt(p2))
        L.append("  Available Dates (" + str(len(dates)) + "): " + ", ".join(dates[:8]))
        if len(dates) > 8:
            L.append("    ... and " + str(len(dates)-8) + " more dates")
        L.append("")
else:
    L.append("No one-stop connections from LHR to LOS found.")
    L.append("")

L.append("=" * 80)
L.append("  END OF REPORT")
L.append("=" * 80)

report = "\\n".join(L)
with open("output/flight_options_D006.txt", "w") as fh:
    fh.write(report)
print("REPORT_WRITTEN:" + str(len(report)) + " chars")
print("DIRECT_OUT:" + str(len(direct_out)))
print("DIRECT_RET:" + str(len(direct_ret)))
print("ONESTOP_OUT:" + str(len(onestop_out)))
print("ONESTOP_RET:" + str(len(onestop_ret)))
print("TOTAL_FLIGHTS:" + str(len(flights)))
"""

# Convert to serializable format
def flight_to_dict(f):
    if hasattr(f, 'model_dump'):
        return f.model_dump()
    elif hasattr(f, '__dict__'):
        return {k: str(v) for k, v in f.__dict__.items() if not k.startswith('_')}
    else:
        return str(f)

def process_results(results):
    processed = []
    if hasattr(results, 'data'):
        results = results.data
    if isinstance(results, str):
        return results
    if hasattr(results, '__iter__'):
        for item in results:
            if isinstance(item, (list, tuple)):
                pair = [flight_to_dict(leg) for leg in item]
                processed.append(pair)
            else:
                processed.append(flight_to_dict(item))
    return processed

out_data = process_results(outbound)
ret_data = process_results(returns)

output = {
    "outbound_flights": out_data,
    "return_flights": ret_data
}

print(json.dumps(output, indent=2, default=str))

from typing import Dict
import tau2.domains.airline.data_model as dm

# Use permissive Dict[str, int] for ALL models that have prices or available_seats
models_to_patch = []
for name in dir(dm):
    obj = getattr(dm, name)
    if isinstance(obj, type) and hasattr(obj, '__annotations__'):
        annots = obj.__annotations__
        patched = False
        if 'prices' in annots:
            annots['prices'] = Dict[str, int]
            patched = True
        if 'available_seats' in annots:
            annots['available_seats'] = Dict[str, int]
            patched = True
        if patched:
            models_to_patch.append(name)

print(f"Patched models: {models_to_patch}")

# Rebuild all patched models
for name in models_to_patch:
    obj = getattr(dm, name)
    if hasattr(obj, 'model_rebuild'):
        obj.model_rebuild(force=True)

# Rebuild parent models
dm.Flight.model_rebuild(force=True)
dm.FlightDB.model_rebuild(force=True)

# Now load
from tau2.domains.airline.tools import AirlineTools
db = dm.FlightDB.load()
tools = AirlineTools(db)

airports = tools.list_all_airports()
print(airports)

from tau2.domains.airline.data_model import FlightDB
from tau2.domains.airline.tools import AirlineTools

db = FlightDB.load()
tools = AirlineTools(db)

# Search outbound one-stop flights
outbound = tools.search_onestop_flight(origin='LOS', destination='LHR', date='2024-07-15')
# Search return one-stop flights
ret = tools.search_onestop_flight(origin='LHR', destination='LOS', date='2024-07-20')

def serialize(obj):
    if hasattr(obj, 'model_dump'):
        return obj.model_dump()
    elif isinstance(obj, list):
        return [serialize(x) for x in obj]
    elif isinstance(obj, tuple):
        return [serialize(x) for x in obj]
    elif isinstance(obj, dict):
        return {k: serialize(v) for k, v in obj.items()}
    else:
        return str(obj)

out_data = serialize(outbound)
ret_data = serialize(ret)

result = {
    "outbound_flights": out_data,
    "return_flights": ret_data
}

with open('flight_search_results.json', 'w') as f:
    json.dump(result, f, indent=2, default=str)

print(json.dumps(result, indent=2, default=str)[:8000])
print("\\n--- SAVED TO flight_search_results.json ---")

search_script = """import sqlite3
import json

conn = sqlite3.connect('world.db')
conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
c = conn.cursor()

# Get all airports
c.execute('SELECT DISTINCT origin FROM flights UNION SELECT DISTINCT destination FROM flights')
airports = sorted([r[0] for r in c.fetchall()])
print(f"All airports ({len(airports)}): {airports}")

# Check if LOS and LHR exist
has_los = 'LOS' in airports
has_lhr = 'LHR' in airports
print(f"LOS: {has_los}, LHR: {has_lhr}")

# Get flights table columns
c.execute('PRAGMA table_info(flights)')
flight_cols = [r[1] for r in c.fetchall()]
print(f"Flight columns: {flight_cols}")

# Find flights from LOS to LHR (direct)
c.execute("SELECT * FROM flights WHERE origin='LOS' AND destination='LHR'")
direct_los_lhr = [dict(r) for r in c.fetchall()]
print(f"Direct LOS->LHR flights: {len(direct_los_lhr)}")

# Find flights from LHR to LOS (direct)
c.execute("SELECT * FROM flights WHERE origin='LHR' AND destination='LOS'")
direct_lhr_los = [dict(r) for r in c.fetchall()]
print(f"Direct LHR->LOS flights: {len(direct_lhr_los)}")

# Find one-stop flights LOS->X->LHR
c.execute('''
    SELECT f1.flight_number as leg1_flight, f1.origin as leg1_origin, f1.destination as leg1_dest,
           f1.scheduled_departure_time_est as leg1_dep, f1.scheduled_arrival_time_est as leg1_arr,
           f1.dates_json as leg1_dates,
           f2.flight_number as leg2_flight, f2.origin as leg2_origin, f2.destination as leg2_dest,
           f2.scheduled_departure_time_est as leg2_dep, f2.scheduled_arrival_time_est as leg2_arr,
           f2.dates_json as leg2_dates
    FROM flights f1
    JOIN flights f2 ON f1.destination = f2.origin
    WHERE f1.origin = 'LOS' AND f2.destination = 'LHR'

report_script = """import sqlite3
import json

conn = sqlite3.connect('world.db')
c = conn.cursor()

# Get flight columns
c.execute("PRAGMA table_info(flights)")
fcol_info = c.fetchall()
fcol_names = [r[1] for r in fcol_info]

# Get all flights
c.execute("SELECT * FROM flights")
all_flights = []
for row in c.fetchall():
    d = dict(zip(fcol_names, row))
    for k, v in d.items():
        if isinstance(v, str) and v.strip().startswith('{'):
            try:
                d[k] = json.loads(v)
            except:
                pass
    all_flights.append(d)

# Index by origin
by_origin = {}
by_dest = {}
for f in all_flights:
    by_origin.setdefault(f.get('origin',''), []).append(f)
    by_dest.setdefault(f.get('destination',''), []).append(f)

def get_avail_dates(f):
    dates_data = f.get('dates', {})
    if not isinstance(dates_data, dict):
        return []
    avail = []
    for dt, info in dates_data.items():
        if isinstance(info, dict) and info.get('status') == 'available':
            econ = None
            prices = info.get('prices', {})
            if isinstance(prices, dict):
                econ = prices.get('economy')
            avail.append({'date': dt, 'economy_price': econ, 'prices': prices})
    avail.sort(key=lambda x: x['date'])
    return avail

def fmt_prices(prices):
    if not isinstance(prices, dict):
        return 'N/A'
    parts = []
    for cls in ['basic_economy', 'economy', 'premium_economy', 'business', 'first']:
        if cls in prices and prices[cls] is not None:
            parts.append(f"{cls.replace('_',' ').title()}: ${prices[cls]}")
    return ' | '.join(parts) if parts else 'N/A'

# Direct flights LOS -> LHR
direct_out = [f for f in all_flights if f.get('origin') == 'LOS' and f.get('destination') == 'LHR']

script = """import sqlite3
import json

conn = sqlite3.connect("world.db")
c = conn.cursor()
c.execute("PRAGMA table_info(flights)")
fcols = [r[1] for r in c.fetchall()]
c.execute("SELECT * FROM flights")
flights = []
for row in c.fetchall():
    d = dict(zip(fcols, row))
    for k, v in d.items():
        if isinstance(v, str) and v.strip().startswith("{"):
            try:
                d[k] = json.loads(v)
            except:
                pass
    flights.append(d)
conn.close()

by_origin = {}
for f in flights:
    by_origin.setdefault(f.get("origin", ""), []).append(f)

def avail(f):
    dd = f.get("dates", {})
    if not isinstance(dd, dict):
        return []
    r = []
    for dt, info in dd.items():
        if isinstance(info, dict) and info.get("status") == "available":
            r.append((dt, info.get("prices", {})))
    r.sort()
    return r

def pfmt(prices):
    if not isinstance(prices, dict):
        return "N/A"
    p = []
    for c in ["basic_economy","economy","premium_economy","business","first"]:
        if c in prices and prices[c] is not None:
            p.append(c.replace("_"," ").title() + ": $" + str(prices[c]))
    return " | ".join(p) if p else "N/A"

direct_out = [f for f in flights if f.get("origin")=="LOS" and f.get("destination")=="LHR"]
direct_ret = [f for f in flights if f.get("origin")=="LHR" and f.get("destination")=="LOS"]

onestop_out = []
for f1 in by_origin.get("LOS", []):
    hub = f1.get("destination", "")
    if hub == "LHR":
        continue
    for f2 in by_origin.get(hub, []):
        if f2.get("destination") == "LHR":
            d1 = {a[0] for a in avail(f1)}
            d2 = {a[0] for a in avail(f2)}
            cd = sorted(d1 & d2)
            if cd:
                onestop_out.append((f1, f2, cd))

onestop_ret = []
for f1 in by_origin.get("LHR", []):
    hub = f1.get("destination", "")
    if hub == "LOS":
        continue
    for f2 in by_origin.get(hub, []):
        if f2.get("destination") == "LOS":
            d1 = {a[0] for a in avail(f1)}
            d2 = {a[0] for a in avail(f2)}
            cd = sorted(d1 & d2)
            if cd:
                onestop_ret.append((f1, f2, cd))

def finfo(f):
    return f.get("flight_id", f.get("id", "?"))

def airline(f):
    return f.get("airline", "?")

def dep(f):
    return f.get("scheduled_departure_time_est", "?")

def arr(f):
    return f.get("scheduled_arrival_time_est", "?")

L = []
L.append("=" * 80)
L.append("  FLIGHT OPTIONS REPORT - SALES TRIP")
L.append("  Deal: D006 | Deal Value: $120,000")
L.append("=" * 80)
L.append("")
L.append("Passenger:        James Okafor")
L.append("Trip Type:        Round Trip (One-Stop)")
L.append("Preferred Cabin:  Economy")
L.append("Time Preference:  Morning flights")
L.append("")
L.append("-" * 80)
L.append("OUTBOUND: Lagos (LOS) -> London Heathrow (LHR)")
L.append("-" * 80)
L.append("")

if direct_out:
    L.append("=== DIRECT FLIGHTS ===")
    L.append("")
    for f in direct_out:
        av = avail(f)
        L.append("Flight: " + finfo(f) + " | Airline: " + airline(f))
        L.append("  Departure: " + dep(f) + " | Arrival: " + arr(f))
        if av:
            L.append("  Available Dates (" + str(len(av)) + "):")
            for a in av[:10]:
                L.append("    " + a[0] + " - " + pfmt(a[1]))
            if len(av) > 10:
                L.append("    ... and " + str(len(av)-10) + " more dates")
        else:
            L.append("  No available dates")
        L.append("")
else:
    L.append("No direct flights from LOS to LHR.")
    L.append("")

if onestop_out:
    L.append("=== ONE-STOP CONNECTIONS ===")

    for i, (f1, f2, dates) in enumerate(onestop_out[:15]):

else:
    L.append("No one-stop connections from LHR to LOS found.")
    L.append("")

L.append("=" * 80)
L.append("  END OF REPORT")
L.append("=" * 80)

report = "\\n".join(L)
with open("output/flight_options_D006.txt", "w") as fh:
    fh.write(report)
print("REPORT_WRITTEN:" + str(len(report)) + " chars")
print("DIRECT_OUT:" + str(len(direct_out)))
print("DIRECT_RET:" + str(len(direct_ret)))
print("ONESTOP_OUT:" + str(len(onestop_out)))
print("ONESTOP_RET:" + str(len(onestop_ret)))
print("TOTAL_FLIGHTS:" + str(len(flights)))
"""
write_result = await write_file("./gen_report.py", script)
print(write_result)

run_result = await run_command("python ./gen_report.py 2>&1")
print(f"Run result: '{run_result}'")

Override the DB path\n# with CUGA_WORLD_DB.\n\nSOURCE_SKILL = "tau2Airline"\nDB_PATH_ENV = "CUGA_WORLD_DB"\n\n# world.db `users.loyalty_tier` uses a shared vocabulary; tau2 membership is a\n# closed set. "standard" (the shared default) is tau2\'s "regular".\n_TIER_TO_MEMBERSHIP = {"standard": "regular"}\n_MEMBERSHIP_TO_TIER = {"regular": "standard"}\n\n# world.db is cross-domain: a few reservation rows carry cabin/trip values from\n# other skills\' vocabularies (e.g. "premium_economy"). tau2\'s schema is a closed\n# set, so coerce anything outside it to the nearest valid tau2 value on read.\n_TAU2_CABINS = {"business", "economy", "basic_economy"}\n_TAU2_FLIGHT_TYPES = {"one_way", "round_trip"}\n\n\ndef _world_db_path() -> Path:\n    override = os.environ.get(DB_PATH_ENV)\n    if override:\n        return Path(override)\n    for candidate in (Path.cwd() / "world.db", Path("/workspace/world.db")):\n        if candidate.exists():\n            return candidate\n    return Path.cwd() / "world.db"\n\n\ndef _connect() -> sqlite3.Connection:\n    conn = sqlite3.connect(str(_world_db_path()))\n    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\n    return conn\n\n\ndef _split_name(full: str) -> Dict[str, str]:\n    parts = (full or "").split(" ", 1)\n    return {"first_name": parts[0], "last_name": parts[1] if len(parts) > 1 else ""}\n\n\n\nMembershipLevel = Annotated[\n    Literal["gold", "silver", "regular"], Field(description="Membership level")\n]\n\n\nclass AirportCode(BaseModel):\n    iata: str = Field(description="IATA code")\n    city: str = Field(description="City name")\n\n\nAirportInfo = Annotated[list[AirportCode], Field(description="Airport information")]\n\n\nclass Name(BaseModel):\n    first_name: str = Field(description="The person\'s first name")\n    last_name: str = Field(description="The person\'s last name")\n\n\nclass Address(BaseModel):'}}

{'id': '80e032c2', 'parent_ids': [], 'type': 'Tool Call', 'content': {'tool_name': 'read_file', 'tool_arguments': {'arg_0': './schema_check.py'}, 'tool_output': 'import sqlite3\nimport json\n\nconn = sqlite3.connect(\'world.db\')\nc = conn.cursor()\n\n# List all tables\nc.execute("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type=\'table\'")\ntables = [r[0] for r in c.fetchall()]\nprint("Tables:", tables)\n\n# For each table, show columns and row count\nfor t in tables:\n    c.execute(f"PRAGMA table_info({t})")\n    cols = [(r[1], r[2]) for r in c.fetchall()]\n    c.execute(f"SELECT COUNT(*) FROM {t}")\n    cnt = c.fetchone()[0]\n    print(f"\\n=== {t} ({cnt} rows) ===")\n    for name, typ in cols:\n        print(f"  {name} ({typ})")\n\n# Sample flight row with full detail\nc.execute("SELECT * FROM flights LIMIT 1")\nfcols = [d[0] for d in c.description]\nrow = c.fetchone()\nif row:\n    print("\\n=== Sample flight row ===")\n    for col, val in zip(fcols, row):\n        sv = str(val)[:400] if val else "NULL"\n        print(f"  {col}: {sv}")\n\n# Unique airports\nc.execute("SELECT DISTINCT origin FROM flights")\norigins = sorted([r[0] for r in c.fetchall() if r[0]])\nc.execute("SELECT DISTINCT destination FROM flights")\ndests = sorted([r[0] for r in c.fetchall() if r[0]])\nprint(f"\\nOrigins: {origins}")\nprint(f"Destinations: {dests}")\n\n# LHR flights\nc.execute("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM flights WHERE origin=\'LHR\' OR destination=\'LHR\'")\nprint(f"Flights involving LHR: {c.fetchone()[0]}")\n\n# Sample reservation\ntry:\n    c.execute("SELECT * FROM reservations LIMIT 1")\n    rcols = [d[0] for d in c.description]\n    rrow = c.fetchone()\n    if rrow:\n        print("\\n=== Sample reservation ===")\n        for col, val in zip(rcols, rrow):\n            sv = str(val)[:400] if val else "NULL"\n            print(f"  {col}: {sv}")\nexcept Exception as e:\n    print(f"No reservations table: {e}")\n\nconn.close()\n'}}

{'id': '20bf559e', 'parent_ids': [], 'type': 'Tool Call', 'content': {'tool_name': 'read_file', 'tool_arguments': {'arg_0': './workspace/docs/q3_report.md'}, 'tool_output': '# Meridian Analytics — Q3 2026 Business Report\n\n**Period:** July 1 – September 7, 2026\n**Prepared by:** Rachel Kim, VP of Sales | Claire Fontaine, CFO\n**Distribution:** Executive Team\n\n---\n\n## Executive Summary\n\nQ3 2026 marks another strong quarter for Meridian Analytics. Across our 15-person team we\nclosed 14 deals out of 22 opportunities, generating **$1,040,000** in new\ncontract value. The sales pipeline remains healthy with several high-value deals in the\npending stage. Customer support ticket volume held steady, with critical issues resolved\nsame-day in all cases.\n\n---\n\n## Sales Performance\n\nTotal closed revenue for the quarter reached **$1,040,000**, with the **South**\nregion leading all territories at **$468,000** in won deals. Our three-person\nfield sales team — James Okafor, Sofia Delgado, and Marcus Webb — collectively worked\n22 active opportunities during the period.\n\nProduct mix shifted toward Meridian Insights Pro, which accounted for the majority of\nclosed revenue. Meridian DataBridge continues to serve as a strong land-and-expand vehicle\nwith several upsell opportunities maturing in Q4.\n\nWin rate for the quarter stood at **63.6%**, slightly above the company\ntarget of 55%. Three deals totalling approximately $240,000 remain in pending status and\nare expected to close by end of September.\n\n---\n\n## Key Highlights\n\n- **Top deal:** Sofia Delgado closed a $198,000 Meridian Insights Pro contract with a\n  Southern-region enterprise customer on September 5 (D019).\n- **Team headcount:** Meridian Analytics closes Q3 at 15 employees across five departments:\n  Sales (4), Engineering (5), Product (3), HR (1), and Finance (2).\n- **Support SLA:** All critical-priority tickets (TKT-004, TKT-011, TKT-015) were resolved\n  within 24 hours of creation.\n- **License utilisation:** SKU-001 (Meridian Insights Pro) is at 94% capacity — a\n  procurement review is scheduled for October.\n\n---\n\n## Next Steps\n\n1. Close the three pending deals (D007, D013, D020, D022) before Q3 end.\n2. Begin Q4 pipeline review — target $1.2M in new ARR.\n3. Resolve the open support tickets (TKT-013, TKT-016, TKT-019) ahead of quarterly\n   customer success calls.\n4. Conduct a license capacity review for SKU-001 and SKU-003 in early October.\n5. HR to initiate two new engineering hire approvals with Kenji Obi to support Q4 roadmap.\n'}}
{'id': '611b8879', 'parent_ids': [], 'type': 'Tool Call', 'content': {'tool_name': 'read_file', 'tool_arguments': {'arg_0': './workspace/docs/meeting_notes_2026_09.txt'}, 'tool_output': 'Q3 REVIEW MEETING — MEETING NOTES\n==================================\nDate:      Monday, September 8, 2026\nTime:      10:00 – 11:30 am PT (Zoom)\nFacilitator: Rachel Kim\n\nATTENDEES\n---------\nRachel Kim        (VP of Sales)\nClaire Fontaine   (CFO)\nPriya Nair        (CTO)\nHannah Park       (Head of Product)\nKenji Obi         (HR Manager)\nJames Okafor      (Account Executive)\nSofia Delgado     (Account Executive)\nDaniel Torres     (Product Manager)\nOscar Mensah      (Finance Analyst)\n\nAGENDA\n------\n1. Q3 Sales Review\n2. Engineering & Product Update\n3. Finance Snapshot\n4. HR Update\n5. Action Items / Q4 Planning\n\n---\n\n1. Q3 SALES REVIEW\n-------------------\nRachel Kim opened with a summary of Q3 performance.\n\n- Total revenue closed (won deals): $1,040,000 across 14 closed-won deals.\n- 22 total deals worked in the quarter; win rate 63.6%.\n- South region led all territories at $468,000 in closed revenue.\n- Largest single deal: D019 — Sofia Delgado — $198,000 — Meridian Insights Pro\n  (signed September 5, Southern enterprise account).\n- Pipeline carry-over into Q4: D007 ($7,800), D013 ($105,000), D020 ($115,000),\n  D022 ($11,000) — total pending ~$239,300.\n\nJames Okafor noted that the North region pipeline is especially strong heading into Q4,\nwith two new prospects from the BostonTech conference (see EX001 travel expense).\n\nAction: Rachel to circulate updated forecast by EOD September 9.\n\n2. ENGINEERING & PRODUCT UPDATE\n---------------------------------\nPriya Nair reported that the DataBridge connector reached 28/30 license utilisation\n(SKU-003) and a capacity upgrade is under evaluation for Q4.\n\nHannah Park flagged that Custom Dashboard Builder (SKU-009) is at 22/25 seats; renewal\nin February 2027 should include a seat expansion.\n\nDaniel Torres confirmed the new Meridian Connector - REST (SKU-005) rollout is complete.\nEleven of twenty available licenses are now provisioned.\n\nThree open support tickets (TKT-013, TKT-016, TKT-019) were reviewed. Liam Chen and\nTom Reyes are owners; target closure by September 12.\n\n3. FINANCE SNAPSHOT\n--------------------\nClaire Fontaine presented a brief Q3 finance summary.\n\n- Five unapproved expense items remain outstanding (EX005, EX010, EX012, EX020, EX023,\n  EX025). Total: ~$1,050. Oscar Mensah to chase approvals by September 10.\n- Hardware spend is tracking within budget. SKU-013 (HIPAA Compliance Pack) renews\n  October 31 at $15,000 — renewal decision needed by September 26.\n\n4. HR UPDATE\n-------------\nKenji Obi confirmed headcount is stable at 15. Two engineering hire requisitions will be\nsubmitted to the board in Q4 to support the roadmap expansion outlined by Priya.\n\nNew joiner orientation materials (see onboarding_guide.md) have been refreshed for the\nupdated tool stack.\n\n5. ACTION ITEMS\n----------------\n| Owner           | Action                                              | Due          |\n|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------------|--------------|\n| Rachel Kim      | Circulate updated Q4 sales forecast                 | Sep 9, 2026  |\n| Oscar Mensah    | Chase outstanding expense approvals (EX005 et al.)  | Sep 10, 2026 |\n| Liam Chen       | Close TKT-013, TKT-016                              | Sep 12, 2026 |\n| Tom Reyes       | Close TKT-019, TKT-020                              | Sep 12, 2026 |\n| Hannah Park     | Initiate SKU-003 capacity upgrade request           | Sep 15, 2026 |\n| Claire Fontaine | Prepare HIPAA pack renewal decision memo (SKU-013)  | Sep 26, 2026 |\n| Kenji Obi       | Submit Q4 engineering hire requisitions             | Oct 1, 2026  |\n\nNEXT MEETING: Q4 Kick-off — Monday, October 6, 2026, 10:00 am PT\n'}}
{'id': '57cba57d', 'parent_ids': [], 'type': 'Tool Call', 'content': {'tool_name': 'read_file', 'tool_arguments': {'arg_0': './workspace/docs/onboarding_guide.md'}, 'tool_output': '# Meridian Analytics — Employee Onboarding Guide\n\nWelcome to Meridian Analytics! This guide covers everything you need for a smooth first\nweek. If anything is unclear, reach out to your manager or HR.\n\n---\n\n## Day 1 Setup\n\n### Accounts & Access\n- [ ] Receive your Meridian email (`<firstname>.<lastname>@meridiananalytics.io`) from IT\n- [ ] Set up Google Workspace (Gmail, Calendar, Drive)\n- [ ] Activate your Slack account and join `#general`, `#engineering`, `#announcements`\n- [ ] Log in to the Meridian Analytics platform at `app.meridiananalytics.io`\n- [ ] Set up 1Password (password manager) — your vault invite arrives by email\n- [ ] Enable MFA on all company accounts before Day 2\n\n### Physical / Badge\n- [ ] Collect your office keycard from Kenji Obi (HR Manager) — desk 4B, second floor\n- [ ] Sign the equipment acceptance form for your assigned laptop\n- [ ] Take a building safety briefing with the office manager\n\n### Tools to Install\n| Tool | Purpose |\n|------|---------|\n| Slack | Team communication |\n| Zoom | Video calls |\n| GitHub | Source code (Engineering) |\n| Figma | Design collaboration (Product/Engineering) |\n| Notion | Internal documentation |\n\n---\n\n## Week 1 Tasks\n\n- [ ] 1:1 with your direct manager (Day 1, 30 min)\n- [ ] Team introduction call — attend `#standup` at 9:30 am daily\n- [ ] Read the Company Handbook in Notion (link shared on Day 1)\n- [ ] Complete Security Awareness training (mandatory, ~45 min)\n- [ ] Complete GDPR & Data Handling training (mandatory, ~30 min)\n- [ ] Shadow a colleague in your team for half a day\n- [ ] Submit your signed offer letter copy and ID documents to Kenji Obi\n- [ ] Set up your direct deposit and benefits enrolment in Rippling (deadline: Day 5)\n\n---\n\n## Key Contacts\n\n| Name | Role | Department | Email |\n|------|------|------------|-------|\n| Kenji Obi | HR Manager | HR | k.obi@meridiananalytics.io |\n| Priya Nair | CTO | Engineering | p.nair@meridiananalytics.io |\n| Rachel Kim | VP of Sales | Sales | r.kim@meridiananalytics.io |\n| Hannah Park | Head of Product | Product | h.park@meridiananalytics.io |\n| Claire Fontaine | CFO | Finance | c.fontaine@meridiananalytics.io |\n\nFor IT issues: open a ticket in the `#it-help` Slack channel.\n\n---\n\n## Policies Summary\n\n- **Working hours:** Core hours are 10 am – 4 pm local time. Flexible outside these times.\n- **Expenses:** Submit expenses within 30 days of purchase via Ramp. Meals > $75 require\n  prior approval. Hardware purchases > $300 require manager sign-off.\n- **PTO:** 20 days per year (accrued monthly). Submit requests in Rippling ≥ 5 business\n  days in advance for planned leave.\n- **Remote work:** Fully remote-friendly. Office available Tuesday–Thursday.\n- **Confidentiality:** All employees sign an NDA on Day 1. Do not share customer data,\n  deal information, or financial figures outside the company.\n- **Code of Conduct:** Reviewed during Week 1 training. Zero tolerance for harassment.\n\nFor the full policy list see the Company Handbook in Notion.\n'}}

{'id': '02613e2a', 'parent_ids': [], 'type': 'Tool Call', 'content': {'tool_name': 'read_file', 'tool_arguments': {'arg_0': './skills/tau2Airline/src/tau2/domains/airline/tools.py', 'start_line': '1', 'end_line': '80'}, 'tool_output': '"""Toolkit for the airline reservation system."""\n\nfrom copy import deepcopy\nfrom typing import List, Optional\n\nfrom loguru import logger\n\nfrom tau2.domains.airline.data_model import (\n    AirportCode,\n    AirportInfo,\n    CabinClass,\n    Certificate,\n    DirectFlight,\n    Flight,\n    FlightDateStatus,\n    FlightDateStatusAvailable,\n    FlightDB,\n    FlightInfo,\n    FlightType,\n    Insurance,\n    Passenger,\n    Payment,\n    Reservation,\n    ReservationFlight,\n    User,\n)\nfrom tau2.environment.toolkit import ToolKitBase, ToolType, is_tool\n\n# TODO: Add an abstract base class for the tools\n\n\nclass AirlineTools(ToolKitBase):  # Tools\n    """All the tools for the airline domain."""\n\n    db: FlightDB\n\n    def __init__(self, db: FlightDB) -> None:\n        super().__init__(db)\n\n    def _get_user(self, user_id: str) -> User:\n        """Get user from database."""\n        if user_id not in self.db.users:\n            raise ValueError(f"User {user_id} not found")\n        return self.db.users[user_id]\n\n    def _get_reservation(self, reservation_id: str) -> Reservation:\n        """Get reservation from database."""\n        if reservation_id not in self.db.reservations:\n            raise ValueError(f"Reservation {reservation_id} not found")\n        return self.db.reservations[reservation_id]\n\n    def _get_flight(self, flight_number: str) -> Flight:\n        """Get flight from database."""\n        if flight_number not in self.db.flights:\n            raise ValueError(f"Flight {flight_number} not found")\n        return self.db.flights[flight_number]\n\n    def _get_flight_instance(self, flight_number: str, date: str) -> FlightDateStatus:\n        """Get flight instance from database."""\n        flight = self._get_flight(flight_number)\n        if date not in flight.dates:\n            raise ValueError(f"Flight {flight_number} not found on date {date}")\n        return flight.dates[date]\n\n    def _get_flights_from_flight_infos(\n        self, flight_infos: List[FlightInfo]\n    ) -> list[FlightDateStatus]:\n        """Get the flight from the reservation."""\n        flights = []\n        for flight_info in flight_infos:\n            flights.append(\n                self._get_flight_instance(flight_info.flight_number, flight_info.date)\n            )\n        return flights\n\n    def _get_new_reservation_id(self) -> str:\n        """Get a new reservation id.\n        Assume each task makes at most 3 reservations\n\n        Returns:'}}
{'id': 'af599c2c', 'parent_ids': [], 'type': 'Tool Call', 'content': {'tool_name': 'read_file', 'tool_arguments': {'arg_0': './skills/tau2Airline/src/tau2/domains/airline/policy.md'}, 'tool_output': "# Airline Agent Policy\n\nThe current time is 2024-05-15 15:00:00 EST.\n\nAs an airline agent, you can help users **book**, **modify**, or **cancel** flight reservations. You also handle **refunds and compensation**.\n\nBefore taking any actions that update the booking database (booking, modifying flights, editing baggage, changing cabin class, or updating passenger information), you must list the action details and obtain explicit user confirmation (yes) to proceed.\n\nYou should not provide any information, knowledge, or procedures not provided by the user or available tools, or give subjective recommendations or comments.\n\nYou should only make one tool call at a time, and if you make a tool call, you should not respond to the user simultaneously. If you respond to the user, you should not make a tool call at the same time.\n\nYou should deny user requests that are against this policy.\n\nYou should transfer the user to a human agent if and only if the request cannot be handled within the scope of your actions. To transfer, first make a tool call to transfer_to_human_agents, and then send the message 'YOU ARE BEING TRANSFERRED TO A HUMAN AGENT. PLEASE HOLD ON.' to the user.\n\n## Domain Basic\n\n### User\nEach user has a profile containing:\n- user id\n- email\n- addresses\n- date of birth\n- payment methods\n- membership level\n- reservation numbers\n\nThere are three types of payment methods: **credit card**, **gift card**, **travel certificate**.\n\nThere are three membership levels: **regular**, **silver**, **gold**.\n\n### Flight\nEach flight has the following attributes:\n- flight number\n- origin\n- destination\n- scheduled departure and arrival time (local time)\n\nA flight can be available at multiple dates. For each date:\n- If the status is **available**, the flight has not taken off, available seats and prices are listed.\n- If the status is **delayed** or **on time**, the flight has not taken off, cannot be booked.\n- If the status is **flying**, the flight has taken off but not landed, cannot be booked.\n\nThere are three cabin classes: **basic economy**, **economy**, **business**. **basic economy** is its own class, completely distinct from **economy**.\n\nSeat availability and prices are listed for each cabin class.\n\n### Reservation\nEach reservation specifies the following:\n- reservation id\n- user id\n- trip type\n- flights\n- passengers\n- payment methods\n- created time\n- baggages\n- travel insurance information\n\nThere are two types of trip: **one way** and **round trip**.\n\n## Book flight\n\nThe agent must first obtain the user id from the user. \n\nThe agent should then ask for the trip type, origin, destination.\n\nCabin:\n- Cabin class must be the same across all the flights in a reservation. \n\nPassengers: \n- Each reservation can have at most five passengers. \n- The agent needs to collect the first name, last name, and date of birth for each passenger. \n- All passengers must fly the same flights in the same cabin.\n\nPayment: \n- Each reservation can use at most one travel certificate, at most one credit card, and at most three gift cards. \n- The remaining amount of a travel certificate is not refundable. \n- All payment methods must already be in user profile for safety reasons.\n\nChecked bag allowance: \n- If the booking user is a regular member:\n  - 0 free checked bag for each basic economy passenger\n  - 1 free checked bag for each economy passenger\n  - 2 free checked bags for each business passenger\n- If the booking user is a silver member:\n  - 1 free checked bag for each basic economy passenger\n  - 2 free checked bag for each economy passenger\n  - 3 free checked bags for each business passenger\n- If the booking user is a gold member:\n  - 2 free checked bag for each basic economy passenger\n  - 3 free checked bag for each economy passenger\n  - 4 free checked bags for each business passenger\n- Each extra baggage is 50 dollars.\n\nDo not add checked bags that the user does not need.\n\nTravel insurance: \n- The agent should ask if the user wants to buy the travel insurance.\n- The travel insurance is 30 dollars per passenger and enables full refund if the user needs to cancel the flight given health or weather reasons.\n\n## Modify flight\n\nFirst, the agent must obtain the user id and reservation id. \n- The user must provide their user id. \n- If the user doesn't know their reservation id, the agent should help locate it using available tools.\n\nChange flights: \n- Basic economy flights cannot be modified.\n- Other reservations can be modified without changing the origin, destination, and trip type.\n- Some flight segments can be kept, but their prices will not be updated based on the current price.\n- The API does not check these for the agent, so the agent must make sure the rules apply before calling the API!\n\nChange cabin: \n- Cabin cannot be changed if any flight in the reservation has already been flown.\n- In other cases, all reservations, including basic economy, can change cabin without changing the flights.\n- Cabin class must remain the same across all the flights in the same reservation; changing cabin for just one flight segment is not possible.\n- If the price after cabin change is higher than the original price, the user is required to pay for the difference.\n- If the price after cabin change is lower than the original price, the user is should be refunded the difference.\n\nChange baggage and insurance: \n- The user can add but not remove checked bags.\n- The user cannot add insurance after initial booking.\n\nChange passengers:\n- The user can modify passengers but cannot modify the number of passengers.\n- Even a human agent cannot modify the number of passengers.\n\nPayment: \n- If the flights are changed, the user needs to provide a single gift card or credit card for payment or refund method. The payment method must already be in user profile for safety reasons.\n\n## Cancel flight\n\nFirst, the agent must obtain the user id and reservation id. \n- The user must provide their user id. \n- If the user doesn't know their reservation id, the agent should help locate it using available tools.\n\nThe agent must also obtain the reason for cancellation (change of plan, airline cancelled flight, or other reasons)\n\nIf any portion of the flight has already been flown, the agent cannot help and transfer is needed.\n\nOtherwise, flight can be cancelled if any of the following is true:\n- The booking was made within the last 24 hrs\n- The flight is cancelled by airline\n- It is a business flight\n- The user has travel insurance and the reason for cancellation is covered by insurance.\n\nThe API does not check that cancellation rules are met, so the agent must make sure the rules apply before calling the API!\n\nRefund:\n- The refund will go to original payment methods within 5 to 7 business days.\n\n## Refunds and Compensation\nDo not proactively offer a compensation unless the user explicitly asks for one.\n\nDo not compensate if the user is regular member and has no travel insurance and flies (basic) economy.\n\nAlways confirms the facts before offering compensation.\n\nOnly compensate if the user is a silver/gold member or has travel insurance or flies business.\n\n- If the user complains about cancelled flights in a reservation, the agent can offer a certificate as a gesture after confirming the facts, with the amount being $100 times the number of passengers.\n\n- If the user complains about delayed flights in a reservation and wants to change or cancel the reservation, the agent can offer a certificate as a gesture after confirming the facts and changing or cancelling the reservation, with the amount being $50 times the number of passengers.\n\nDo not offer compensation for any other reason than the ones listed above."}}

{'id': '35477e41', 'parent_ids': ['e2744cdd'], 'type': 'Tool Call', 'content': {'tool_name': 'read_file', 'tool_arguments': {'arg_0': './skills/tau2Airline/src/tau2/environment/toolkit.py', 'start_line': '1', 'end_line': '40'}, 'tool_output': 'from enum import Enum\nfrom typing import Annotated, Any, Callable, Dict, Optional, TypeVar\n\nfrom pydantic import BaseModel, Field\n\nfrom tau2.environment.db import DB\nfrom tau2.environment.tool import Tool, as_tool\nfrom tau2.utils import get_dict_hash, update_pydantic_model_with_dict\n\nTOOL_ATTR = "__tool__"\nTOOL_TYPE_ATTR = "__tool_type__"\n\n\nT = TypeVar("T", bound=DB)\n\n\nclass ToolKitType(type):\n    """Metaclass for ToolKit classes."""\n\n    def __init__(cls, name, bases, attrs):\n        func_tools = {}\n        for name, method in attrs.items():\n            if isinstance(method, property):\n                method = method.fget\n            if hasattr(method, TOOL_ATTR):\n                func_tools[name] = method\n\n        @property\n        def _func_tools(self) -> Dict[str, Callable]:\n            """Get the tools available in the ToolKit."""\n            all_func_tools = func_tools.copy()\n            try:\n                all_func_tools.update(super(cls, self)._func_tools)\n            except AttributeError:\n                pass\n            return all_func_tools\n\n        cls._func_tools = _func_tools\n\n'}}
